title: OpsIQ Proof-Level Matrix
purpose: A single, ordered ladder of proof strength. Every capability in OPSIQ_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.json is assigned its HIGHEST honestly-achieved level. A higher level does not erase lower ones — it includes them. UI-surfaced (L15) is the gold standard; most OpsIQ capabilities are backend + CI + audit proven (L10–L13) but NOT yet owner-visible in UI, and the ledger says so plainly.
rule: A capability may be assigned level N only if every claim at level N is backed by named source/test/CI/audit evidence in the repo. Absent evidence, it is assigned the highest level actually proven — never the level aspired to.

levels.meaning: No code exists for this capability.
Deterministic implementation exists but has no automated test.
Pure deterministic unit tests pass (happy path).
A Zod schema / invariant rejects incoherent output, and a test proves it fails closed.
Hostile/negative unit tests pass (tamper, skip, no-evidence, no-fabrication, no-hidden-score).
Service layer tested (authorization / persistence behaviour with a test double).
Persists to a real Postgres and is verified in a *.db.test.ts (TEST_WITH_DB=true).
Evidence/approval/authorization gating verified against a real DB (EVIDENCE_REQUIRED / OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED).
Cross-workspace/tenant isolation verified against a real DB.
The DB proof runs in the REQUIRED CI lane (LANE_B) on every PR, verified by log inspection — not a generic green.
Proven as part of a full multi-stage pipeline simulation (e.g. interpret → resolve → prioritise → explain → survive → recover) DB-backed.
Has a dedicated audit directory with matrices + an evidence ledger under docs/audits/.
Survived a hostile, full-repo adversarial audit pass without being downgraded.
Exposed through a real API route an owner/manager can call.
Surfaced in a real UI an owner actually sees and acts on.

honestNotes: L7–L11 are the strongest OpsIQ proof today: real Postgres + gating + isolation + required CI + pipeline.
L14/L15 (owner-callable API / owner-visible UI) are the most common GAP: many capabilities are backend-and-CI-proven but not yet UI-surfaced. That gap is stated, never hidden.

No level in this ladder implies real-world business outcome (money earned, business saved). Outcome is NOT a proof level here because OpsIQ has no verified real-world outcome data — see OPSIQ_PUBLIC_CLAIMS_FORBIDDEN.md.
